We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research the officially documented context window and output token limits of the current Claude and GPT model families. Cite the vendors' own documentation pages and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

I'll research the officially documented context window and output token limits for current Claude and GPT models, citing only from the vendors' own documentation.

## Claude Models

Based on Anthropic's documentation, here are the current Claude model specifications:

SOURCE: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows.md | QUOTE: "Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Mythos Preview have a 1M-token context window." | CLAIM: These Claude models have 1M token context windows

SOURCE: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows.md | QUOTE: "A single request to any of them can generate up to 128k output tokens (`max_tokens`)." | CLAIM: Claude models with 1M token context can generate up to 128k output tokens

SOURCE: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows.md | QUOTE: "Other Claude models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5, have a 200k-token context window." | CLAIM: Older Claude models have 200k token context windows

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Fable 5.1 - 1M tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Fable 5.1 has 1M token context window

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Sonnet 5.5 - 1M tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Sonnet 5.5 has 1M token context window

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Opus 4.6 - 500K tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Opus 4.6 has 500k token context window in some plans

SOURCE: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8606394-how-large-is-the-context-window-on-paid-claude-plans | QUOTE: "Claude Sonnet 4.6 - 500K tokens" | CLAIM: Claude Sonnet 4.6 has 500k token context window in some plans

## GPT Models

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Official OpenAI documentation for GPT-4o, GPT-4, and GPT-3.5 context window sizes
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Official OpenAI documentation for GPT model output token limits
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Official OpenAI documentation for GPT-4 Turbo context window specifications

## Uncertain Section

I was unable to find current, official OpenAI documentation with specific context window sizes and output token limits for their GPT model family. The OpenAI documentation I could access appears to require authentication or doesn't contain the specific numerical limits you're asking for. The Claude documentation is comprehensive and clearly states both context window sizes (1M tokens for current models, 200k for older ones) and output token limits (128k for 1M-context models), but I cannot provide equivalent verified information for GPT models from OpenAI's official sources.
